articles.title: Boxing: Lee Reeves dies aged 31, three months after Dublin fight
articles.summary: Irish boxer Lee Reeves has died aged 31, three months after he suffered serious injuries in a bout in Dublin, his promoter Queensberry has announced.
articles.body:
Irish boxer Lee Reeves has died aged 31, three months after he suffered serious injuries in a bout in Dublin, his promoter Queensberry has announced.

Reeves was fighting Gary Cully for the vacant BUI Celtic light-welterweight title on 1 August but was knocked out in the 10th round at the 3Arena.

The Limerick southpaw was carried out of the ring on a stretcher after the fight and admitted to hospital in a "criticial but stable" condition.

He underwent surgery and had been in a ​medically induced coma since.

Jonathan O'Brien, Reeves' friend and coach, led tributes, saying he "fought so hard till the end".

"Goodbye son, sleep tight, you fought so hard till the end. We love you so much, rest in peace with your mam and brother waiting at the heavenly gates. Look over your sisters and your father, give them the strength to get through this. We love you Lee," O'Brien posted on Instagram.

Reeves, who was nicknamed 'El Champo' turned professional in 2018 and he won 16 of his 18 bouts in the ranks.

He spent large parts of his early professional career fighting in Canada and Colombia, and impressive performances across the United Kingdom and Ireland led him to face Cully in Dublin in August.

Reeves was knocked down twice in the 10th round and was carried out of the ring.

Outside of boxing, Reeves - who lost his mum, Cathy, to suicide - was an ambassador for the Limerick Treaty Suicide Prevention group.

He also appeared on the BBC reality show Survivor in 2023, which saw contestants stranded on a desert island.

Cully, Reeves' opponent in his last bout, said on Instagram they had known each other for years.

"I still remember the stadium days when I used to watch Lee in the nationals, the weight above me, and [I would] always be impressed by his fights and his flashy gear," he said.

"What a character and a gent. It's never been nothing but love between us champ, can't really believe I'm writing this but RIP brother."

Family friend and Limerick City councillor Catherine Slattery also paid tribute to Reeves: "Limerick is a very dark place tonight with the loss of Lee Reeves. Lee was not just a boxer that excelled in his career - he was a mental health advocate who highlighted mental health and how it can affect young people," she said.

"Lee was a very proud Limerick man, he loved Limerick and its people and any chance he got to promote Limerick, he took it.

"Lee loved his family. He was very proud of his dad, Tony, and he adored his sisters and his nieces and nephews and they, in return, adored him.

"Lee had great faith in God and the only [consolation] is that Lee's mam and brother are embracing him in their arms in heaven.

"The loss of Lee will be felt in Limerick for a long time to come and I am heartbroken for Lee that he lost his fight.

"Rest in peace El Champ - you will be missed by us all."

articles.title: UFC: Amanda Nunes calls for Kayla Harrison rematch at featherweight
articles.summary: Amanda Nunes calls for a rematch against Kayla Harrison at featherweight after defeat by the UFC bantamweight champion on Saturday.
articles.body:
Amanda Nunes has called for a rematch against Kayla Harrison at featherweight after defeat by the UFC bantamweight champion on Saturday.

The Brazilian former double champion lost on her return to action after a three-year absence, submitted by American Harrison in the fourth round.

Nunes, 38, has a long history with Harrison, having been training partners, and posted on social media she is chasing a rematch at the weight class above.

"145 [pounds] rematch," Nunes wrote. "Accepted."

Nunes said before UFC 334 she intended to continue fighting even in defeat, while Harrison suggested it could be her last contest in MMA.

Harrison, 36, had neck and spinal surgery just 10 months ago and has been open about the difficulties of making 135lb (9st 9lb).

She said after her win she was considering hanging up her gloves.

"I've got a lot of decisions to make when I get home," Harrison said.

"Every time I make weight, I say 'never again'. So we'll see."

Harrison is unbeaten in her four fights in the UFC and has just one loss on her record, a 2022 loss to Larissa Pacheco in the PFL.

Asked if there was any other fight other than the Nunes rematch that would interest her, Harrison said: "If Ronda [Rousey] wants to come get some. It'd be fun. Free money."

articles.title: Jorge Linares: Former world champion detained by ICE in Texas
articles.summary: Three-time world champion Jorge Linares says he has been detained by US Immigration authorities in Texas.
articles.body:
Former three-weight world champion Jorge Linares says he has been detained by US immigration authorities in Texas.

The 41-year-old Venezuelan posted a message on social media on Sunday about being held by America's Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agency.

Linares is based in Miami and has fought more than 10 times in America.

"ICE has me at the Texas border crossing. This is crazy," wrote Linares. , external

He retired after being beaten by Britain's Jack Catterall in a light-welterweight bout in October 2023 in the last of his 56 fights.

A renowned fighter, he won 47 of his bouts and claimed world titles at featherweight, super-featherweight and lightweight in a distinguished career which started in 2002.

"I can confirm that my friend Jorge Linares, former WBA world champion, is in ICE custody," said WBA president Gilberto Mendoza , external on social media.

"Immigration attorneys are handling his case, and I am in constant contact with his family.

"As WBA president, I will always support our champions, in and out of the ring. Stay strong, Jorge."

The AFP news agency reported a statement from Wilner & O'Reilly, an immigration law firm representing Linares, which said he was "legally present in the United States and has co-operated fully with the authorities".

They added: "We are working closely with ICE and the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to resolve this matter as quickly as possible.

"We are confident in Mr. Linares' legal position and expect this matter to be resolved once the process has concluded. We ask his supporters, the press and the public for patience in the meantime."

articles.title: UFC: Eight released from prison following Usman Nurmagomedov-Merab Dvalishvili brawl
articles.summary: The eight people who received prison sentences for their part in a mass brawl involving MMA fighters Usman Nurmagomedov and Merab Dvalishvili have been released.
articles.body:
The eight people who received prison sentences for their part in a mass brawl involving MMA fighters Usman Nurmagomedov and Merab Dvalishvili have been released.

Last week, former UFC bantamweight champion Dvalishvili and PFL lightweight champion Nurmagomedov were involved in a mass brawl in Abu Dhabi, which led to 10 arrests.

A video of the incident appeared to show Russian Nurmagomedov slap Dvalishvili after approaching the Georgian from behind.

Fighting then broke out between the two and members of their teams in a hotel lobby.

The Abu Dhabi Criminal Court sentenced , external eight of those arrested to six months in prison, along with a fine and a deportation order following their jail terms.

But in a new statement , external , the court said "the revised penalty" was now a fine for each defendant.

Eight sentenced to jail over Nurmagomedov-Dvalishvili brawl

Nurmagomedov slaps Dvalishvili to spark hotel brawl

Abu Dhabi news outlet the National reported , external Nurmagomedov was one of those released along with seven of his associates.

"The ruling is consistent with the legal framework governing the criminal case and considers the settlement between the parties and their withdrawal of mutual claims and disputes arising from the incident," the statement read.

"The court had previously convicted six defendants of disturbing public security, spreading panic and endangering people's lives, while two others were convicted of using information technology to film and publish footage of the brawl online."

Dvalishvili released a video after the incident calling Nurmagomedov and his team "snakes" as he received treatment on his bloodied face.

He later posted a message on X , external saying he hoped the authorities would "release everyone" and that he would not be pressing charges.

The Georgian fought at the Real American Freestyle (RAF) event in the United Arab Emirates on Saturday, where he beat Brazilian Marlon Moraes.

articles.title: Usman Nurmagomedov released from UAE prison after hotel brawl arrest
articles.summary: Russian MMA fighter and seven associates still face deportation after a hotel fight with other MMA fighters.
articles.body:
Usman Nurmagomedov has been released from a prison in the United Arab Emirates and faces deportation from the country after a brawl in a hotel lobby that led to his arrest, the Abu Dhabi Judicial Department says.

The Russian mixed martial arts (MMA) fighter, who was arrested in the UAE capital last week along with seven associates, had his sentence reduced after reconciliation, the department said on Tuesday.

“Eight defendants’ sentences were reduced in hotel brawl case after reconciliation and victim’s appeal to Abu Dhabi Government for their release,” it said in a statement posted on social media.

According to reports in UAE media, the court also ordered all to be deported after serving their sentences.

The fighter and his associates also had their fines reduced.

They were initially sentenced to six months in prison and fined 300,000 dirhams ($81,688) each, but their fines have now been halved, reports said.

Last week, the Abu Dhabi Criminal Court convicted 10 people over the mass brawl, which involved Nurmagomedov, Georgian MMA fighter Merab Dvalishvili and their teammates at a hotel.

The brawl broke out before a wrestling event organised ⁠⁠by Real American Freestyle (RAF) where Nurmagomedov’s brother, Umar, and Dvalishvili were due to fight against different opponents.

The brawl broke out on Wednesday when Dvalishvili, who was scheduled to appear at RAF Abu Dhabi on Saturday, was being interviewed in the lobby of the Yas Hilton.

PFL lightweight champion Usman Nurmagomedov, the cousin of retired MMA legend Khabib Nurmagomedov, and his associates approached Dvalishvili. Videos shared online showed ‌‌Usman coming in from behind and slapping Dvalishvili, which started the melee.

Usman was not scheduled to feature on the RAF Abu Dhabi card but travelled to the UAE to accompany his older brother, Umar, who was scheduled to face Urijah Faber.

Later on Friday, the event organisers removed Umar from the card, replacing him ‌‌with ‌‌Saba Lazishvili, Dvalishvili’s friend who was also involved in the brawl.

articles.title: Lee Reeves Dies at 31 After Being Injured in Boxing Title Fight vs. Gary Cully
articles.summary: Irish boxer Lee Reeves died at the age of 31, Queensberry Promotions confirmed on Tuesday, per the Associated Press.
articles.body:
Irish boxer Lee Reeves died at the age of 31, Queensberry Promotions confirmed on Tuesday, per the Associated Press .

Reeves' death comes over three months after he was hospitalized following a knockout from fellow Irishman Gary Cully in the final round of their Boxing Union of Ireland Celtic super-lightweight title fight at the 3Arena in Dublin on Aug. 1.

"Everyone at Queensberry is devastated to learn of the passing of Lee Reeves," Queensberry Promotions said in a statement.

"Lee was an immensely talented boxer, as well as a true role model and inspiration to his community," the statement added. "Our deepest condolences go to Lee's family, friends and all those who loved him. We ask that their privacy be respected at this incredibly difficult time. Rest in peace, Lee."

After the knockout loss, Reeves received initial treatment in the ring before being carried out on a stretcher. Queensberry said at the time that his condition was critical but stable.

Reeves had a professional boxing record of 16-2 with 11 knockout victories. In addition to his boxing career, he worked as a model and appeared on Survivor UK in 2023.

articles.title: Jon Jones Slams Josh Hokit on Social Media After Ciryl Gane's Win in UFC 334 Main Event
articles.summary: Former UFC heavyweight champion Jon Jones isn't letting up in his feud with Josh Hokit following his loss to current titleholder Ciryl Gane in the main event of UFC 334 this past Saturday.
articles.body:
Former UFC heavyweight champion Jon Jones isn't letting up in his feud with Josh Hokit following his loss to current titleholder Ciryl Gane in the main event of UFC 334 this past Saturday.

Jones fired back at Hokit in a series of tweets, blasting his calls for an immediate rematch over an inadvertent eye poke in the first round and criticizing his fighting style.

Hokit posted several tweets explaining why he deserves an immediate rematch, but he might not get his wish. All three judges scored the fight for Gane, who overcame an early storm and pulled away in the championship rounds to retain his title.

Jones didn't buy any of his claims, and he pushed back on the notion that Gane sustained more damage in the fight.

Hokit eventually began responding to Jones, who maintained his stance that the 29-year-old didn't do enough to win the fight. He also taunted him with his 2023 win over Gane by first-round submission.

Jones and Hokit train at the same gym in New Mexico, but it's clear that there's no love lost between them. Jones retired from MMA in the summer of 2025, so they won't be settling their differences in the Octagon anytime soon.

It can be expected that Jones' barbs will add extra fuel to Hokit's fire as he tries to work his way back to a title shot.

articles.title: UFC Qatar adds last-minute matchup just four days before showtime
articles.summary: Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) sure likes short-notice fights. This weekend’s UFC Qatar card was locked and loaded with 11 fights. Now, just four days...
articles.body:
Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) sure likes short-notice fights .

This weekend's UFC Qatar card was locked and loaded with 11 fights. Now, just four days before showtime, matchmakers have added a Lightweight matchup between two promotional newcomers.

Former Professional Fighters League (PFL) competitor John Mitchell will collide with FightStar Championship Lightweight champion Shoaib Yousaf this weekend (Sat., Nov. 21, 2026) inside Ali Bin Hamad al-Attiyah Arena in Doha, Qatar.

Mitchell (11-3) made five appearances under the PFL banner, compiling a 3-2 record. His most notable setback came against Jakub Kaszuba in the inaugural PFL Europe Lightweight tournament final.

The 31-year-old Irishman has since returned to the win column, knocking out Kallew dos Santos in just 59 seconds at Cage Conflict 18 in July.

Mitchell owns a 54 percent finishing rate, with four knockouts and two submissions among his 11 professional victories.

Yousaf (14-3), meanwhile, enters his UFC debut riding a six-fight winning streak. "The Assassin" has finished each of his last three opponents by first-round knockout, most recently stopping Tariel Abbasov in September.

The 31-year-old Englishman has competed for Cage Warriors, Brave CF, OKTAGON MMA and Absolute Championship Berkut (ACB) throughout his career. Yousaf owns 10 finishes — eight knockouts and two submissions — with all eight of his knockout victories coming in the opening round.

Neither fighter will have the benefit of a traditional UFC training camp or much time to prepare specifically for the other. However, four days' notice is considerably better when both men are entering under the same circumstances.

articles.title: Aljamain Sterling is 'dying' from weight cut for UFC Qatar
articles.summary: Aljamain Sterling can't believe he ever made 135 pounds to compete in bantamweight title fights.
articles.body:
Aljamain Sterling admittedly was not in good shape Tuesday during an interview with MMA Junkie. Simply asking the former UFC bantamweight champion how he's doing yielded a brutally honest response.

"Dying," Sterling said through his hoarse-sounding voice. "I'm dying."

Sterling (26-5 MMA, 18-5 UFC) meets Kevin Vallejos (18-1 MMA, 4-0 UFC) in the featherweight co-main event Saturday at UFC Fight Night 294 ( Paramount+ ) from ABHA Arena in Doha, Qatar. It's not that Sterling's weight cut is brutal for a specific reason, so much as it's just reached an inevitable stage three days before he steps on the scale to make 146 pounds.

"When you start to get down to a certain percentage of body fat, you feel it no matter how well you did the diet," Sterling said. "That's where I'm at."

In times like this, Sterling – who fought in five UFC bantamweight title fights, including three title defenses, between 2021 and 2023 – can't believe he ever cut down to 135 pounds.

"It really is (unfathomable)," Sterling said. "It's actually crazy to me when I think about it. I go, 'How? How?' I just want to know how I did that. What type of mental fortitude did I have that allowed me to do something so insane?"

Sterling said he's "been a featherweight for a long time. I just didn't know it." It wasn't until a UFC Performance Institute test before his division debut in April 2024 that he realized just how much muscle he was shedding to reach 135.

"That just gave me the clarity that I am big enough, I'm definitely strong enough, I train with 145ers religiously, so why not go up?" Sterling said. "That gave me the confidence I needed to make the jump."

Now No. 4 in the latest Meta UFC rankings, Sterling will enter UFC Fight Night 294 on a two-fight winning streak after defeating Brian Ortega and Youssef Zalal. A third consecutive victory over No. 10 Vallejos could be enough to secure a title shot vs. featherweight champ Alexander Volkanovski .
authors: Simon Samano and Mike Bohn, MMA Junkie

articles.title: WBC boss Mauricio Sulaiman 'absolutely' supports Agit Kabayel title unification for Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua winner
articles.summary: Tyson Fury meets Anthony Joshua for the WBA 'super' heavyweight title on December 11, while Agit Kabayel puts the WBC belt on the line against Nelson Hysa on November 28; WBC president Mauricio Sulaiman will "absolutely" back a unification with the Fury-AJ winner next
articles.body:
Agit Kabayel will defend his WBC heavyweight title against Nelson Hysa on November 28, and if he successfully defends his belt the WBC will "absolutely" be in favour of a meeting with the winner of the huge all-British heavyweight showdown on December 11.

Fury vs Joshua could have been a final eliminator for the WBC title, though Fury and Joshua will now box for the WBA 'super' heavyweight championship.

"It was a natural final elimination for the mandatory, one against two [in the rankings], but the promoters did not request the fight to be a final elimination and they chose to do [it for] another organisation's title," WBC president Mauricio Sulaiman told Sky Sports .

"The industry likes unifications, people like to see undisputed and we don't get in the way. We like to support that."

Kabayel won't be under the obligation of an immediate mandatory defence.

"Kabayel is going to defend at the end of the month and then he is free - we did not mandate any fight [for the winner] because we believe the mandatory contender must be the highest available real mandatory," Sulaiman said.

"We will see if we're going to order a final elimination or if there's a unification or if there's something else that can be done."

articles.title: Boxing: Jorge Linares remains in ICE detention and facing deportation
articles.summary: Former three-weight world champion Jorge Linares remains in the custody of US immigration authorities in Texas and is facing deportation.
articles.body:
Former three-weight world champion Jorge Linares remains in the custody of US immigration authorities in Texas and is facing deportation.

The 41-year-old Venezuelan was detained on Sunday when US Border Force and Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers arrested him at El Paso International Airport.

"On October 26, 2023, he entered the country with permission to stay for a temporary period, but in defiance of our nation's laws, he overstayed his welcome. He will remain in ICE custody pending removal proceedings," said an ICE spokesperson.

"To be clear, a pending application or work authorisation does not confer legal status in the United States."

Linares is based in Miami and has fought more than 10 times in America.

The immigration law firm Wilner & O'Reilly are representing Linares and they denied their client was in the US illegally.

"Mr Linares is authorised to be in the United States and he has cooperated fully with immigration authorities," said a Wilner & O'Reilly statement.

"We are in communication with ICE and are working to resolve this matter as quickly as possible. Immigration matters follow established procedures, and those procedures take time.

"We are confident in Mr. Linares's position and ask his fans, the press and the public for patience in the meantime."

Ex-world champion Linares detained by ICE in Texas

Linares posted a message on social media on Sunday saying that "ICE has me at the Texas border crossing. This is crazy".

He won 47 of his 56 bouts and claimed world titles at featherweight, super-featherweight and lightweight in a distinguished career which started in 2002.

He retired after being beaten by Britain's Jack Catterall in a light-welterweight bout in October 2023 in his last fight.

articles.title: Fury vs Joshua undercard: Jai Opetaia has withdrawn from heavyweight bout with Deontay Wilder on December 11 bill
articles.summary: Australian star Jai Opetaia was due to step up to heavyweight to box Deontay Wilder on the undercard of Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff on December 11; Opetaia has had to withdraw from the contest after aggravating a hand injury
articles.body:
The star Australian cruiserweight was due to step up to heavyweight for the first time and box Wilder on the undercard of Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua on December 11.

But an injury to his hand exacerbated in training has forced him out.

Opetaia's co-promoter Mick Francis said: "On behalf of Jai Opetaia and his team, I can confirm that Jai has unfortunately been forced to withdraw from this scheduled December fight with Deontay Wilder.

"Jai sustained a hand injury during his September bout against Noel Mikaelian and has since aggravated it during training."

Francis added: "This is a disappointing setback for Jai, who was looking forward to what promised to be a cracking fight. His focus now is on making a full recovery and continuing his quest to become the undisputed cruiserweight champion of the world."

Opetaia said: "Apologies to everyone and especially 'Bronze Bomber' and his team for withdrawing from the bout. Fighter to fighter I know the feeling and it's frustrating. I've always prided myself on fighting anyone, any place... It is what it is.

"The goal has never changed and still like I've always said remains the same. Undisputed! They all said I couldn't after signing with Zuffa Boxing, everything always against us, stripped and vacated multiple times ... but you watch.

Wilder however won't have a shortage of potential opponents offering their services as a replacement on the Principality Stadium bill.

Derek Chisora, who fought Wilder in an exciting rumble earlier this year, has publicly declared his interest in fighting on the card.

British heavyweight champion Richard Riakporhe posted on social media to tell Wilder: "I will fight you on less than four weeks' notice. I am ready for 12 full rounds. None of this eight round business, let's go."

Another UK heavyweight, Johnny Fisher also posted: "Wilder in Cardiff? Oh, go on then. Bosh."

Frazer Clarke has called for a battle of Olympic bronze medallists with Wilder too.

articles.title: Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua: Jai Opetaia pulls out of Deontay Wilder fight
articles.summary: Australian Jai Opetaia withdraws from his heavyweight fight with Deontay Wilder on the undercard of Tyson Fury's bout with Anthony Joshua in December.
articles.body:
Australian Jai Opetaia has withdrawn from his heavyweight fight with Deontay Wilder on the undercard of Tyson Fury's bout with Anthony Joshua.

Unbeaten cruiserweight champion Jai Opetaia was set to step up to heavyweight for the first time to face American Wilder at Cardiff's Principality Stadium on 11 December.

Opetaia, 31, did not give a reason for his withdrawal, but it is understood he aggravated a hand injury in training.

"Apologies to everyone and especially [Wilder] and his team for withdrawing from the bout," he wrote on Instagram.

"Fighter to fighter, I know the feeling and it's frustrating. I've always prided myself on fighting anyone, any place."

Opetaia criticised "keyboard warriors" who suggested he was scared off by Wilder's powerful right hand.

Opetaia, who has won all 31 of his professional bouts, reiterated his ambition to become undisputed cruiserweight champion.

Unified champion David Benavidez has expressed an interest in facing Opetaia in 2027.

Opetaia's withdrawal leaves a significant gap on the undercard of one of the biggest all-British heavyweight fights in history.

It remains unclear whether former world champion Wilder, 41, will still feature on the bill, but several British heavyweights have expressed an interest in replacing Opetaia.

Derek Chisora has offered to face Wilder in a rematch, having lost a split decision in London in April.

Richard Riakporhe, Olympic bronze medallist Frazer Clarke and Johnny Fisher have said they would be prepared to fight.

The long-awaited showdown between Fury and Joshua is understood to be for the WBA 'super' heavyweight title, with ring walks expected to take place no earlier than 01:00 GMT on 12 December.

articles.title: Lauren Price: Welsh boxer gets chance to become undisputed world champion
articles.summary: Lauren Price gets chance to become Wales' first undisputed world champion in her fight with Michaela Kotaskova in Cardiff.
articles.body:
Lauren Price has a shot at becoming Wales' first undisputed world champion against Michaela Kotaskova on Friday after the vacant WBO welterweight title was added to the fight.

The 32-year-old will go up against Czech Republic's Kotaskova in Cardiff in a fight that will be shown live on BBC Two and BBC iPlayer.

Price will defending her IBF, WBA and WBC belts at Utilita Arena and will now have the chance to add a fourth.

Mikaela Mayer has relinquished the WBO title before her rematch with Chantelle Cameron in December.

Olympic champion Price successfully defended her belts and moved to a 10-0 record by beating mandatory challenger Stephanie Pineiro on points in April.

Live on BBC Two Wales and iPlayer from 21:00 GMT

If she wins, Price - who also holds the IBO and Ring Magazine belts - will become the first Welsh boxer to hold all four major world titles simultaneously.

Joe Calzaghe beat Mikkel Kessler for the WBO, WBA and WBC super-middleweight titles in 2007 but had relinquished the IBF title.

Price would be the fourth British female fighter to achieve undisputed status after Savannah Marshall, Chantelle Cameron and Ellie Scotney.

American Mayer held the WBO welterweight title but will instead go up against Cameron for her unified WBO, WBA, and WBC super-welterweight belts.

"As much as I looked forward to unifying for undisputed, it's dragged out too long and the Cameron rematch is now my priority," she posted on social media.

"No need to be holding up the welterweight division in the meantime."

Price was told of the decision late on Tuesday, and says it has added a further incentive as she prepares to face Kotaskova.

"It will mean a little bit more history," said Price. "And it just hits home a little bit because it would mean I'd achieved everything I set out to do in boxing.

"As an amateur, it was to go and win an Olympic gold. As a pro it's to become undisputed world champion. If get that win on Friday night I will have ticked every accolade there is.

"I've got the chance to grab that with both hands and I'm adamant I'm not only keeping the belts in Wales, I'm adding one."

Price faces a tough test against 34-year-old Kotaskova, who is the current WBF title holder and has not been beaten at welterweight.

Her only defeat in a 15-fight professional career came at the weight above, when she lost on points to Chantelle Cameron in a three-minute-round bout.

Kotsakova called the opportunity to fight for undisputed status "a huge surprise" that offers a chance to create history in her homeland.

In a warning to Price, she said: "It won't be easy for her. I have followed her career for many years and I saw in her last fight the first time there wasn't a big difference between fighters.

"Nobody's perfect; every fighter has some weaknesses and there's always a way to win. I see a chance."

Cardiff's Kronk? The gym where Welsh champions train

The boxer who lost 45kg and fought depression to chase a dream

Price's fight with Kotaskova headlines a bill featuring plenty of Welsh fighters, including Rhys Edwards going for the WBA continental featherweight title against Scotland's Lee McGregor, a former British and European champion.

"Friday night is about Welsh boxing. Lauren is creating opportunities for Welsh boxers," said promoter Ben Shalom.

"There are many more nights to come and they will get bigger and bigger."

Shalom also claimed Edwards could soon be headlining bills of his own, but 29-year-old McGregor warned: "A lot of people think I'm past it and are writing me off, but I'm determined to prove a lot of people wrong."

Meanwhile, Willy Gilheaney faces Argentina's Alberto Ignacio Palmetta for the WBA continental gold welterweight belt.

articles.title: Rico Verhoeven: Could the kickboxing superstar step in to fight Deontay Wilder on the Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua bill?

articles.body:
Wilder was due to box Jai Opetaia at the Principality Stadium on December 11, but Opetaia had to withdraw from their heavyweight bout and will stay at cruiserweight.

Wilder will remain on the card but the race is on to select a new opponent for him.

Rico Verhoeven could be a viable candidate. A kickboxing superstar, earlier this year the Dutchman went straight into a world title fight with legendary Ukrainian Oleksandr Usyk.

Verhoeven performed surprisingly well in that WBC championship fight in Giza. Although he was stopped in the 11th round, he had looked to threaten a monumental upset.

The Dutchman is now considering his next move and his team didn't rule out stepping in for Opetaia to fight Wilder in December.

"Plenty of interesting things happening right now," Verhoeven's manager Karim Erja told Sky Sports .

"We're exploring some exciting options for Rico, but you know him, he's always up for a big fight.

"Let's see what happens in the coming few days."

articles.title: Ilia Topuria: "No tengo la más mínima duda de que Aleksandre se proclamará campeón del Mundo..."
articles.standfirst: 'El Conquistador' pelea este fin de semana en UFC Qatar
articles.summary: 'El Conquistador' pelea este fin de semana en UFC Qatar
articles.body: Las expectativas en torno a Aleksandre Topuria (7-1) son altísimas pero Ilia Topuria (17-1), su hermano menor y doble campeón de la UFC, no tiene la menor duda sobre que las cumplirá. 'El Conquistador' vuelve al octágono de UFC este fin de semana para medirse al mexicano Santiago Luna (8-1), este sábado en Qatar. Será su tercera pelea en UFC, llegando con dos victorias acumuladas. Una buena racha que lo coloca a las puertas de aspirar al top-15 del peso gallo. El primer paso, desde luego, para pensar en aspiraciones más grandes. Pero Ilia apunta alto, muy alto, con el futuro de Aleksandre: "No tengo la más mínima duda de que se proclamará campeón del mundo". Y hasta señala un periodo temporal: "En 2028 o principios de 2029". "He entrenado con mucha gente, pero nunca he entrenado con nadie tan técnico como mi hermano ni con nadie que tenga el mismo nivel de conocimientos y comprensión de este deporte. Y, de verdad, no lo digo solo porque sea mi hermano", añade el 'Matador' en una entrevista en 'La Gazzetta de Georgia'. Aleksandre, está claro, necesita actividad. Él quiere pelear mínimo dos veces al año pero las diferentes circunstancias lo hicieron imposible este 2026. Qatar puede ser, de nuevo, la rampa de despegue para una prometedora carrera en la UFC. "Creo que Sandro y yo nos parecemos mucho en muchos aspectos, aunque tengamos estilos de lucha diferentes. Sandro es como yo. A los dos nos cuesta más enfrentarnos a luchadores con menos técnica. Porque cuando alguien no tiene técnica, en realidad es mucho más difícil, ya que son impredecibles. Nunca sabes de dónde va a venir un golpe", analiza, además, Ilia Topuria, refiriéndose a su hermano como 'Sandro' de forma cariñosa. De momento, Santiago Luna es la próxima parada en el ascenso de 'El Conquistador'.

articles.title: Kevin Holland Confesses to Intentionally Fouling One of His Former Opponents
articles.summary: Kevin Holland is coming off a controversial majority draw against Uros Medic at UFC 334, with confusing scorecards that included a point deduction against Me...
articles.body:
Kevin Holland is coming off a controversial majority draw against Uros Medic at UFC 334, with confusing scorecards that included a point deduction against Medic for a low blow in the second round. Despite having a point taken, all three judges had the round 10-9 before the deductions, bringing it to a 9-9 round. Holland endured two low blows and reflected on how it affected his fight.

While appearing on The Ariel Helwani Show , Holland was discussing the low blows he had taken when Helwani pulled up a post by Uros Medic. The post claimed Holland was faking the second low blow.

Holland responded, saying, "Oh no, brother. No reason to fake it. I don't understand why I would need to fake it. I was whooping his a**. I mean at the end of the day, if you go back and watch the fight, same thing with the Mike Malott fight. Up until the moment that these guys start to land the low blow, and I'm not talking about the first one, I'm talking about the second one, I'm piecing them up, dude."

This led Holland to reminisce about other low blows, and in perfect Kevin Holland fashion, the 170-pounder admitted something almost no other fighter has ever done: he admitted to intentionally low-blowing one of his previous opponents.

Who did Kevin Holland intentionally low blow?

Holland, who has taken a good number of low blows, wondered whether he takes more because he is tall, or because he thinks the opponent aims for a low blow when they start losing. He admitted that during his fight with Marvin Vettori, he aimed for a low blow. Holland told Helwani, "That one time when I kicked Marvin Vettori in the b**** really, really hard, it wasn't an accident."

When Helwani asked why he did it, Holland responded, "I mean, it was crazy too, because it was like I was piecing him up, right? Like pow, pow, pow, and he just had this look in his face, and I was like, I don't like this dude. He was talking all that c*** the day before."

This is a wild admission for Holland, even if the fight took place way back in 2021 . It begs the question whether more fighters have intentionally aimed for a low blow, but Holland is the only one who admits it. Holland has always been known for his antics in the cage, most famously talking to his opponents, coaches, and even the commentary team during his matches.

The UFC veteran seemed lighthearted about the low blows he has taken, but his admission to intentionally fouling Vettori is not his best moment. While he should be honest about the foul, it would be much better to not intentionally try to end a fight with a low blow.

There have been more serious consequences for fouls in the UFC, especially since 2021, so Holland's story about intentional fouls and the fouls he endured at UFC 334 , leading to a point deduction, serves as a comparison to the state of the sport. By revealing his story about Vettori, it does raise questions about whether other fighters are using fouls as a tactic for ending fights, getting time to recover, or disrupting their opponent's rhythm.

What is next for Kevin Holland after the controversial decision at UFC 334?

While most fighters would only make a wild admission after leaving the company, Kevin Holland is very open about the tactics and intends to stay in the UFC for a great deal longer. He discussed with Helwani his signing of his new contract, but not saying exactly how long the contract is, but that it is "a long one." Holland claimed, "When I'm done with the UFC, I'm done with Mixed Martial Arts."

It seems like Holland will have many more matchups in the UFC, and following the draw at UFC 334, there are many unranked opponents that he may get a matchup with . At this point in his career, Holland is still putting on entertaining and challenging fights, but hopefully he does not engage in any intentional fouls or take any more fouls.

articles.title: Joe Rogan finds one thing 'crazy' about Ciryl Gane's UFC 334 win
articles.summary: Joe Rogan was surprised to see Ciryl Gane get away with an early poke at UFC 334.
articles.body:
Joe Rogan was surprised to see heavyweight champion Ciryl Gane get away with an early poke at UFC 334.

Gane (15-2 MMA, 12-2 UFC) retained his title by outlasting Josh Hokit (10-1 MMA, 4-1 UFC) in this past Saturday's main event at Madison Square Garden. Gane accidentally poked Hokit in the eye in Round 1, which referee Marc Goddard didn't acknowledge. After the fight, Hokit revealed that he was seeing triple . With Gane's history of unintentional fouls, Rogan expected harsher repercussions.

"He didn't even get fined a point, which I thought was crazy," Rogan said of Gane on a recent episode of " The Joe Rogan Experience" podcast. "He does this thing always where you're coming at him, and he does this (extends fingers). You can't do that. You can never do that. I guess in muay Thai it's OK because you've got the gloves on, and they do that all the time. They frame off. It's normal in muay Thai. With fingers, you just can't do that. You should never do that. ...

"You just can't extend your hand toward someone's eyes. That's a point. That should be like grabbing the fence, point. If you poke a guy in the eye, you're doing this (extends fingers), you know you're not supposed to do that. That's the point. It could f*ck a guy's whole career up. Look at (Tom) Aspinall – four f*cking surgeries, man. The guy is the heavyweight champion of the world, and he has to retire his belt because he can't fight right now."

All three judges scored the fight three rounds to two in favor of Gane, which makes Rogan wonder how much a point deduction would have changed things.

"I mean, he won it by one point, which is really crazy when you think about the eye poke because that would have been a draw," Rogan said. "The problem was Goddard didn't see it at the time. A thing like that, I feel like given the history of Ciryl Gane, it's worth a pause in the action. ... Stop it, take a look."

articles.title: Aleksandre Topuria: "No dejo que las expectativas me afecten. Tengo mi propia historia"
articles.standfirst: 'El Conquistador' atiende a MARCA antes de enfrentarse a Santiago Luna en UFC Qatar
articles.summary: 'El Conquistador' atiende a MARCA antes de enfrentarse a Santiago Luna en UFC Qatar
articles.body: Este sábado, un año después de su último combate, Aleksandre Topuria (7-1) vuelve a la jaula más famosa del mundo: la de la UFC. El peleador hispanogeorgiano, hermano mayor de Ilia Topuria, se medirá en Qatar al mexicano Santiago Luna (8-1). Otro prospecto para medir las enormes expectativas que hay en torno a ‘El Conquistador’. Y con ese contexto, buscando escribir su propia historia, ‘Sandro’ atiende a MARCA. Pregunta. Un año después vuelve al sitio en el que lo dejó… ¿cómo se encuentra? R. Súper bien, me siento preparado. Esa es la respuesta, no tengo más que decir. Ahora mismo me siento súper hambriento, súper hambriento, pero estoy bien. Aún así me encuentro súper bien, estamos haciendo las cosas bien. P. Hábleme de su 2026. Cerró el pasado 2025 por todo lo alto, ha sido padre, pasó lo que pasó en la Casa Blanca… Han ocurrido muchas cosas. R. Ha sido un año de mucho aprendizaje. Han pasado cosas, cosas bastante intensas… pero aprendimos muchísimo. Hemos hecho muchísimo. De momento yo diría que ha sido un año bastante importante en mi vida. No siempre van a salir las cosas como uno quiere, pero independientemente de cómo salgan las cosas, siempre hay que mirar también la parte positiva, ¿verdad?. Cuando una vez enfrentes a todos esos momentos difíciles, cuando ya ha terminado todo, miras atrás y dices, ‘vale, independientemente de que ha pasado esto, esto, esto, también ha pasado esto, esto, esto’. Entonces estamos bien, gracias a Dios. P. Recuerdo que, tras ganar a Almakhan, me dijo que le gustaría pelear al menos dos veces en 2026. No se ha cumplido ese objetivo. Entiendo que le hubiera gustado algo diferente… R. Sí, definitivamente. Definitivamente quería hacer dos peleas, como yo creo que te lo he dicho ya. Dos peleas al año para mí está perfecto. Tres peleas al año sería un escenario todavía mejor. Pero así es como sucedieron las cosas, así es como se dio y ya está. Eso es lo que es, aceptamos lo que es. Y no pienso en lo que ha podido pasar, estoy 100% enfocado en lo que tengo por delante. Así que me siento bien y agradecido con lo que me toca vivir. P. Se ha hablado mucho de que Santiago Luna, su rival, tiene más que ganar en esta pelea que usted. Él viene de derrota, usted de dos triunfos… usted tiene más nombre. Podría ‘robarle’ mucho si sale ganador. R. ¿Sabes qué, Irati?. Yo no me enfoco de esa manera. A mí esto de quién está en mejor posición y quién está en peor posición, no dejo que esas cosas me afecten. A nadie lo miro por encima porque vengo de ahí, nadie lo miro desde abajo porque quiera estar ahí… por lo tanto trato de mantener los pies en el suelo y trato de no enfocarme de tal manera porque hace que mis energías se dividan, por lo tanto yo me enfoco de otra manera. Es un rival más que lo tengo por delante y lo tengo que pasar por encima. Punto y final. No me interesa a mí si está por encima, si está por debajo, que luego todo eso ya es trabajo de todos los demás, de pensar, de hacer el cálculo, quién se merece el qué, cómo, quién está por encima de quién, es que éste tenía más para ganar, el otro tenía menos y cosas así, es algo externo. Que si me pongo en plan analítico, podríamos debatir también ese tema, quién está por delante, quién está atrás, pero ahora mismo en este punto donde yo me encuentro, no me enfoco en esas cosas. No me enfoco. Mi enfoque está totalmente en otra cosa. P. ¿Qué tipo de combate espera? Ante Thicknesse y Almakhan controló ambas peleas y se mostró muy cómodo en el ‘striking’ y en la lucha. R. Tengo que llevar el control. Y voy a llevar el control. No voy a pelear la pelea de nadie. Voy a llevar y voy a pelear mi pelea. No me enfoco más en otra cosa, no tengo pensado otra cosa, no me enfoco en a ver cómo me defiendo de esto. No me enfoco en eso. Si hay que plantarse en el medio, porque uno no quiere llevar tu pelea, bueno, bueno… pues lo vamos a hacer. P. Hace unos días, Ilia dijo en una entrevista que lo veía a usted como campeón de la UFC en 2028 o principios de 2029. Merab Dvalishvili, otro ex campeón de UFC, dice lo mismo. ¿Qué significan para usted las expectativas que tienen depositadas en sus posibilidades y futuro? R. A ver, es algo que sale de su boca, ¿verdad? Yo no... Estas cosas nosotros no las conversamos, quiero decir… yo no tengo estas conversaciones con él, que cómo crees que si soy bueno, que si soy malo, etcétera. Entre nosotros es algo muy natural y después como que sucede que hay entrevistas y cada uno dice lo que piensa, ¿verdad?. Así que yo siempre he dicho lo que he pensado de cada uno. Probablemente ellos dicen lo que ellos piensan también de cada uno. Y me alegro de escucharlo, pero tampoco dejo que esas cosas me afecten. Ni tampoco fliparme, ni tampoco tomármelo como una exigencia, como una presión extra. Yo tengo mi propia historia. Ellos opinan lo que opinan. Este es muy bueno, este es malo, este va a ser campeón, etcétera, etcétera. Y es lo que ellos tienen que decir porque esto es lo que ellos piensan. Después es como yo me lo tome… los pies en la tierra. Y esa es mi virtud. Eso es lo que hace que yo esté preparado para lo que venga.

articles.title: Mouslim Saidoulaiev, la joya francesa que crece en Madrid: "No es sólo llegar a UFC, es ir lo más lejos posible"
articles.standfirst: El peleador del Black Panther habla en MARCA antes de debutar como profesional en WOW 34
articles.summary: El peleador del Black Panther habla en MARCA antes de debutar como profesional en WOW 34
articles.body: Pocos nombres hay en las MMA españolas tan prometedores como el de Mouslim Saidoulaiev. El francés, afincado en Madrid y entrenando en el Black Panther desde hace dos años, es campeón amateur en nuestro país y tiene una racha de once triunfos consecutivos. Ganó todo lo posible... y ahora el reto está en el salto a profesional. Debutará este fin de semana, en WOW 34 Valencia. Pregunta. Para quién no lo conozca: ¿Cuál es la historia de Mouslim Saidoulaiev? Respuesta. Nací en Francia, en París. He hecho toda mi vida ahí, pero mis padres son de Chechenia. Yo empecé por el judo desde que tenía cuatro o cinco años, empecé por el judo por mi padre, a él le gustaba mucho todo lo relacionado con las artas marciales. Llegué hasta el cinturón negro. Luego dejé un poco el deporte y a los 19 años empecé con las MMA en Francia. Empecé como amateur y hace dos años vine aquí, a España, a Madrid, para estudiar y también seguir mi carrera. P. Estudia fisioterapia, ¿no? R. Sí, ahora mismo estoy estudiando. La razón principal es para estudiar, pero cuando vine aquí, la primera cosa en la que me fijé era buscar un gimnasio donde pudiera entrenar. Así descubrí el Black Panther. Cuando entré la primera vez ahí, dije: ‘yo quiero entrenar aquí y voy a entrenar aquí’. P. ¿Cómo lo descubrió? R. Estaba yendo a muchos gimnasios, haciendo clases de prueba y un día hablé con un amigo de Francia, porque vive aquí también… y me dijo que conocía a un amigo que iba a un gimnasio. Le dije ‘vale, voy a ver’. Era mi último día aquí, porque vine por una semana para descubrir Madrid, era mi último día, y dije ‘vale, voy a verlo’. Y así fue. P. ¿Y cuál es su plan ahora? Porque ha sido campeón de MMA amateur en España. ¿Le gustaría quedarse aquí? R. La verdad es que todavía no lo he pensado mucho, pero a mí me gusta España, la vida aquí en Madrid está muy bien. Y claro, ahora que estoy en el Black Panther. Me siento muy bien aquí. La verdad es que me veo siguiendo aquí porque tengo todo a mi disposición para crecer y ser cada vez mejor. P. Entiendo que el salto a profesional llega porque ya se le han acabado los retos como amateur… R. Como has dicho, no me quedan muchas cosas en amateur, y yo sentía que era el momento. Después de mi última pelea en WOW, hablé con los entrenadores, me tomé mi tiempo, entrené bien y ajusté muchas cosas. Ahora es lógico que pase a profesional. P. En qué momento de su carrera supo que esta sería su vida, que se dedicaría profesionalmente a las artes marciales mixtas. R. Para mí desde el principio era un objetivo, sé que lo puedo hacer. Pero sí, la primera vez que peleé en WOW… para mí fue una experiencia increíble, me sentí un profesional por el ambiente y todo. Eso me dio un buen empujón. P. Entiendo que el objetivo es hacer carrera en WOW y ser campeón. R. Sería la mejor opción, sería la mejor… pero es que yo no pienso mucho en el futuro, yo ahora mismo, mi futuro es mi pelea en una semana. Claro que sería un objetivo conseguir el cinturón de WOW, pero ahora mismo mi foco está en mi pelea. P. ¿Cómo se define como peleador? Mucha gente, el gran público, lo descubrirá ahora. R. La gente me ve mucho como un wrestler que quiere derribar siempre, pero yo me veo como un peleador que puedo ajustarme, depende de a quién tengo frente a mí, pero yo me puedo ajustar y puedo ganar de cualquier manera. Si tengo que derribar para ganar, lo voy a hacer, si tengo que ir para atrás, solo boxear, lo voy a hacer… yo busco solo ganar, y claro, como en este deporte hay de todo, pues tenemos que adaptarnos. P. ¿Se ve como peso pluma a largo plazo? R. Sí, la verdad que yo creo que siempre voy a ser un peso pluma. Tenemos que ver cómo evoluciona mi cuerpo, pero con el tamaño que tengo… me veo ahí. P. ¿Qué piensa de las expectativas? Hay muchas puestas en usted, se hablan maravillas de su nivel en el gimnasio… y los campeonatos de España amateur lo dejaron bien claro. R. Sí, para mí es más confianza. Es un orgullo, me da mucha confianza que crean eso de mí. Es más una fuerza extra que presión. P. Su objetivo, claro, es la UFC. El objetivo de todo peleador de MMA. R. Sí, la verdad es que sí, llegar a UFC… pero no solo llegar, ir lo más lejos posible. Sé que soy capaz y que lo voy a hacer.

articles.title: Ex-Heavyweight Boxer Goran Gogic Pleads Guilty to Drug Charge and Faces At Least 10 Years in Prison
articles.summary: NEW YORK (AP) — Former heavyweight boxer Goran Gogic pleaded guilty to a drug charge Wednesday, a year after his trial was upended when it was revealed that a juror had been offered a $100,000 bribe to return a not guilty verdict.
articles.body:
NEW YORK (AP) — Former heavyweight boxer Goran Gogic pleaded guilty to a drug charge Wednesday, a year after his trial was upended when it was revealed that a juror had been offered a $100,000 bribe to return a not guilty verdict.

Shackled at the ankles, Gogic, 47, spoke through an interpreter as he admitted conspiring to smuggle 20 tons (18.1 metric tons) of cocaine to Europe from Colombia through U.S. ports using commercial cargo ships.

He pleaded guilty in Brooklyn federal court to conspiracy to violate the Maritime Drug Law Enforcement Act, a charge that carries a mandatory minimum penalty of 10 years in prison and a maximum of life.

Lee Reeves Dies at 31 After Being Injured in Boxing Title Fight vs. Gary Cully

Under the plea agreement Gogic signed with prosecutors, the boxer agreed to forfeit $1 million associated with his crimes.

Prosecutors said they plan to ask at a sentencing scheduled for Feb. 16 that Gogic be ordered to serve 23 years in prison. His lawyer said the former athlete, who is from Montenegro, is likely to be deported when he is released from prison.

Gogic has been described by law enforcement officials as a "major drug trafficker" who operated on a "mammoth scale."

He fought professionally in Germany from 2001 to 2012, compiling a 21-4-2 record, according to boxing website Sport & Note. He was listed as 6-foot-5 (1.96 meters) and weighed in at anywhere from 227 pounds (103 kilograms) to 250 pounds (113 kilograms).

"Gogic stepped outside the ring and into the drug trade, and today justice delivered a knockout blow," U.S. Attorney Joseph Nocella Jr. said in a news release.

Alan Futerfas, Gogic's lawyer, said he had no comment Wednesday.

A year ago, law enforcement authorities arrested three people in a jury tampering plot and alleged one of them called a juror in Gogic's trial multiple times on his cellphone before the juror agreed to meet him on Staten Island.

During the meeting, the man told the juror that associates in the Bronx were willing to pay him to return a not guilty verdict, according to a criminal complaint.

When word of the bribery attempt was reported to court officials, a federal judge abruptly dismissed the jury just as it was about to hear opening statements.

articles.standfirst: El peleador hispanogeorgiano tiene pelea este fin de semana en UFC Qatar
articles.summary: El peleador hispanogeorgiano tiene pelea este fin de semana en UFC Qatar

articles.title: Conor McGregor gives 400 employees a day off for GTA VI launch: ‘Enjoy the game!’
articles.summary: Conor McGregor has announced that 400 employees across his workforce will get Thursday, November 19, off to mark the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI.
articles.body: Conor McGregor has announced that 400 employees across his workforce will get Thursday, November 19, off to mark the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI. The former UFC champion shared the decision in a post on X, telling his employees that they could spend the day playing the long-awaited game. His announcement comes just before Rockstar Games releases GTA VI, which is scheduled to arrive on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S on November 19. McGregor described the offer as a day off for his team working across different countries and continents.Conor McGregor gives 400 employees a day off for GTA VI launchMcGregor shared the announcement on November 18, one day before the game’s release. He made clear that the offer covered his entire workforce, which he put at 400 people. The post did not list the businesses or countries covered by the decision, so the full details of the employees involved remain unclear.“In honor of GTA launching tomorrow, I announce to my entire workforce team, 400 strong across countries and continents, you have your entire day off tomorrow!” McGregor announced.He ended the message with another line for his staff: “Enjoy the game! Your pal, the boss, Conor McGregor Snr.”The announcement gives employees a break on the same day that one of the most awaited video game releases in recent years reaches players. MMAmania, which reported McGregor’s post, noted that the day off would be unpaid. McGregor’s own announcement did not mention whether the time away from work would be paid, making this an important detail from the report.The offer is also notable because it covers more than a single office or a small team. McGregor referred to 400 employees working across countries and continents. However, he did not share further details about how the break would affect the daily operations of his businesses.What players can expect from Grand Theft Auto VIRockstar Games has confirmed that Grand Theft Auto VI will launch on Thursday, November 19, for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. The release date is listed on the game’s official website. The story takes place in the fictional state of Leonida and brings players back to Vice City.The game follows Jason and Lucia, whose plans take a turn after an easy score goes wrong. According to Rockstar Games, the pair find themselves caught in a criminal conspiracy across Leonida and must rely on each other to get through it. The company has also released a launch trailer ahead of the game’s arrival.GTA VI follows Grand Theft Auto V, which was released in 2013. The wait between the two main releases has made November 19 an important date for players who have been looking forward to the next game in the series. The new title will be available on two console platforms at launch.McGregor’s post did not reveal whether he plans to play GTA VI himself. However, his message has given his 400 employees the chance to enjoy the game’s release without having to report to work on Thursday.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: UFC cuts 'surprised' Virna Jandiroba, recent title challenger and No. 3-ranked strawweight

articles.body:
Virna Jandiroba is the latest notable name to be released from the UFC.

Jandiroba, a recent challenger for the UFC strawweight title, announced Wednesday on social media that she has been unexpectedly cut following her UFC Vegas 124 loss to fellow top contender Tatiana Suarez. Jandiroba was the UFC's No. 3-ranked strawweight contender and a winner of six of her past eight appearances at the time of her UFC exit.

Jandiroba said in Portuguese upon revealing the news, translation courtesy of MMA Fighting's Guilherme Cruz :

"I was caught off-guard by this decision at this point in my career. Obviously, we're dealing with a private company, and I knew that everything was very unstable. You can be there one day and gone the next. But given the timing and the circumstances, I was in a good place in my career, so I was surprised in that sense. "I had 14 fights inside the organization, so I experienced a lot of great things there. I achieved my dreams, reached the top of the division, fought for the belt, and shared truly incredible moments with my team. "I had 13 fights before the UFC and 14 in the UFC. In other words, I was already a fighter before joining the UFC, and I'll continue to be one outside the UFC as well. My team, manager, and I are already talking and exploring possibilities. I don't want to retire now. I still have plenty left in the tank. I feel great, I'm eager to fight, extremely excited, and willing to keep learning. I still have a few more fights in me. You'll see me fighting before I retire. I'm optimistic, and I think good things are coming."

I'm optimistic, and I think good things are coming."

As mentioned in her statement, Jandiroba, 38, said she plans to continue competing outside of the UFC.

A former Invicta FC champion, Jandiroba leaves the UFC with a 9-5 promotional record, highlighted by a five-fight win streak from 2022-25 that carried her to a shot at the promotion's undisputed 115-pound title in October 2025 against Mackenzie Dern. Jandiroba ultimately lost a hard-fought decision to Dern, but rebounded with a win over top-15-ranked contender Tabatha Ricci this past April.

In addition to Ricci, Jandiroba also holds UFC wins over current ranked contenders Yan Xiaonan, Amanda Lemos and Loopy Godinez.

Jandiroba is the latest UFC contender to be forced to part ways with the promotion despite her in-cage success, joining recent examples Michael Page, Farid Basharat and Norma Dumont.

articles.title: Prospect Watch: Cayden Griffiths
articles.summary: Cayden Griffiths is on the grind to the top in the gym, on the road, and in the online world.
articles.body:
Prospect Cayden Griffiths will fight in front of his Coachella Valley fans on Friday, November 20 at the Fantasy Springs Resort and Casino, live on DAZN Boxing .

We interviewed the undefeated knockout artist about his path ahead.

Griffiths spoke candidly about the obligations for athletes to build a social media presence.

The path for a promising prospect in professional boxing looks far different than it once did. Instead of developing on deep undercards out of the spotlight, emerging talents are seen worldwide on before-the-bell streams from around the world. They are also expected to build their presence and persona for fans through social media visibility.

We spoke recently with Golden Boy Boxing welterweight prospect Cayden Griffiths , a native of Harrisburg, Pennsylvania, now based in the Coachella Valley at the Diaz Brothers Training Camp in Indio.

With an undefeated record of nine wins, eight by knockout, Griffiths is set to appear in his fourth fight of 2026 on Friday, November 20, in front of his hometown fans at the Fantasy Springs Resort and Casino, airing live on DAZN Boxing. Prelims begin at 5 p.m. ET/2 p.m. PT , with the main card following at 8 p.m. ET/5 p.m. PT . NY Fights will cover the action ringside.

Fighting in your hometown venue can be a blessing and a curse, but Griffiths says he loves it.

"I mean, there's nothing better than fighting in front of your hometown packed-out arena with your family and friends.

"This is the biggest stage for me in my career so far. Biggest fight, biggest opportunity. There's a little bit of pressure, but it's nothing that I haven't been able to withstand before.

"I'm just kind of doing what I always do, just training a little bit harder than I usually do, and making sure everything's going smooth."

Griffiths will face Jean Rivera-Pacheco of Puerto Rico, a 33-year-old with a 10-4 record and one knockout. Rivera-Pacheco has fought as high as middleweight and will present a bigger opponent for Griffiths, who says he's watched video of Rivera-Pacheco to size him up.

Griffith says he is beginning to outgrow welterweight and will use the fight as an opportunity to test himself at a higher division in a fight at super welterweight.

"He's definitely a step up in competition for me, which means that I need to be on my A game. But honestly, I'm more excited for this fight than any of my other ones because I feel like when I'm with those types of fighters that are more skilled and less of a stay-ready fight. I feel like I perform better. I rise to the occasion," said Griffiths, looking forward to his best performance.

"I'm really not looking to play around. I know this guy is tough, so I mean, I'm definitely going to have to be on him from the jump. But I'm just going to have to be smarter about it. I'm not going to be able to go in there and mow everybody down," said Griffiths who notes Rivera-Pacheco is used to taking shots from heavier opponents.

"It's going to be tough to get him out of there. But I think I have the ability and the skills to do so," said Griffiths.

Cayden Griffiths Avoiding Career Missteps

Griffiths knows he needs to avoid the trap faced by young knockout punchers of developing their skills with a minimal number of rounds under the lights in front of a crowd.

But Griffiths is getting some of the best sparring in the world at the Diaz Brothers facility with world champions and prospects from around the world, including a contingent from Uzbekistan, including MJ Akhmadaliev, Shakhram Giasov, Israel Madrimov, and Bektimir Melikuziev.

"I'm sparring with world champions, so I think that kind of gives me experience. And I mean, in a fight, anything can happen," Griffiths pointed out, so he avoids merely trying to go a few rounds and giving an opponent opportunities to survive. "It's boxing. It only takes one punch. And at this point in my career, I'm not a big enough name yet to where I can afford to lose, and I don't want to lose. I hate losing. It's the worst feeling in the world."

"I'm not just a come-forward slugger. You know what I mean? Honestly, I haven't really got to show a lot of my arsenal yet, which is probably a good thing.

"But at the same time, I genuinely feel like there's so much more that I have to show that I'm capable of, and I think this fight will allow me to do so," explained Griffiths.

Griffith says he's aware he can't steamroll his opponents as he steps up in opposition . "That's one of the main reasons why I'm so excited, man. I've genuinely been waiting for this for a while, and you know everything has been kind of falling into place for me. So I'm just blessed to be able to get in there and just smack a dude around," said Griffiths, with a broad smile on his face.

"I'll be fresh on my feet. I'll be ready to go. I'm so excited, just freaking flow in there. I'm feeling like water."

The modern prospect in 2025 has obligations beyond training. Griffiths and his peers are expected to cultivate a social media presence, posting content on multiple platforms and engaging with the public and boxing media (like me) to build a fan base and a positive reputation.

Griffiths was surprisingly candid about the challenge.

"It's definitely tough. When people think social media, they think 'oh, you just go on there and post whatever.' It's really not about that. There's a lot of things that go into it as far as like what time you post, and it's just kind of a hassle, I'm going to be honest.

But Griffiths says at this point, the routine is baked in as part of the job.

"I've been on social media since I was 11 or 12, and since the beginning, I was just trying to market myself on social media.

"I've taken it serious since the beginning, and I mean it's definitely hard to manage, but I feel like now it's becoming repetitive. The more you do something, the more you kind of get used to it. And now I'm starting to understand algorithms and stuff like that. It's a pain in the ass, but it definitely makes a difference," admits Griffiths. He agreed it's not really optional anymore

"I'd say probably 85 to 90% of promoting is done through social media now," estimated Griffith, noting that in previous eras, fighters and fight cards were advertised on television and in promotional items like posters, programs, even hotel room keys and poker chips for major Las Vegas events. As someone who worked through this era, Griffiths is right (and I have a few of those poker chips).

"Now everything's social media oriented, and that's where it's at now. If you don't have a social media, it's hard to really gain a fan base … I mean, you might as well not exist at that point if people can't check you out, find out what you're about. They want to get to know who you are and you know whether they relate to you," said Griffiths.

"I get DMs all the time from people all over the world that are inspired by me. It's crazy to think about because before, TV commercials aren't really global like that. Whereas now, you can post on social media, and people from all over the world will see it. It definitely opens up new doors and new opportunities in other countries," said Griffiths.

For now, the world will have to come to Griffiths, and the high desert is beautiful as winter approaches. Griffiths vs Rivera-Pacheco will be part of the before the bell undercard airing live on DAZN Boxing on Friday, November 20
