articles.title: Merab Dvalishvili’s Teammate Says A Former Title Challenger Threw The Punch Cameras Never Caught
articles.summary: Aljamain Sterling told ESPN that Umar Nurmagomedov punched Merab Dvalishvili after the viral Abu Dhabi hotel brawl video ended. Here’s what he alleged and wh...
articles.body:
There's a new and serious allegation attached to the attacks involving Usman and now Umar Nurmagomedov and Merab Dvalishvili in Abu Dhabi ahead of the RAF event.

Aljamain Sterling, a longtime friend and training partner of Dvalishvili, did an interview with ESPN on November 17 alleging that Umar Nurmagomedov, a UFC bantamweight and the brother of Usman Nurmagomedov, was involved in a second attack that wasn't caught on the viral video.

Usman, a PFL lightweight who has been linked to a potential UFC move, was involved in the viral confrontation at an Abu Dhabi hotel. The footage showed him approaching Dvalishvili and striking him, sparking a brawl that led to multiple people being detained and imprisoned. They have reportedly since been released.

But according to Sterling, there was another attack initiated by Umar Nurmagomedov after the cameras stopped recording.

Sterling, who wasn't there, also alleges that members of the group grabbed and restrained Dvalishvili's teammate Saba Lazishvili and kicked him in the head while he couldn't defend himself.

Sterling used some very serious language, referring to attempted murder in connection with the alleged attack on Lazishvili, and says everyone involved should be punished.

Let's look a little deeper into what Sterling said, what it could mean for the UFC regarding Dvalishvili and the Nurmagomedovs, and the promotion's interest in signing Usman Nurmagomedov. Let's talk UFC.

Abu Dhabi Brawl and Sterling Allegation Key Facts

Hotel lobby brawl, Yas Hilton, Abu Dhabi

Umar punched Dvalishvili after the video ended

Usman and seven associates sentenced to six months, later reduced

Usman and seven associates were initially sentenced to six months and fined. The sentences were reduced after reconciliation between the parties and an appeal to the Abu Dhabi Government. Abu Dhabi's Judicial Department announced Usman's release on Tuesday.

Umar was pulled from the RAF card after the brawl, and Lazishvili took his spot.

What Did Aljamain Sterling Say Umar Nurmagomedov Did?

According to Sterling, Umar's approach to Dvalishvili was done to make it appear as though he was de-escalating the situation and seeking to make amends between the Nurmagomedov family and group and Dvalishvili.

Instead, according to Sterling, he used that opportunity to punch Merab and further attack him.

Sterling told ESPN that Umar "walks up to Merab and punches him in the face." Of the alleged attack on Lazishvili, he said, "I think that's attempted murder."

While what Sterling says is serious, because he wasn't there, it's still a secondhand account.

Dvalishvili and Lazishvili hinted at a second confrontation on The Ariel Helwani Show, but Lazishvili declined to say what happened.

If Dvalishvili is really interested in pursuing any sort of criminal charges or consequences for Umar Nurmagomedov and his family, he'll have to speak up about that attack himself.

Until the full account is substantiated, this is still an allegation from Sterling that remains unproven.

How Will This Affect the Dvalishvili-Nurmagomedov Feud?

It will undoubtedly intensify the feud between Dvalishvili and the Nurmagomedov family, and even Sterling and members of that group.

Dvalishvili beat Umar by unanimous decision at UFC 311 in January 2025, handing him the first loss of his career.

This rivalry has escalated into something that goes way beyond competition, rankings, and championship fights.

It's beyond personal, and while that may make many uncomfortable, and justifiably so, it's something that if the UFC can find a way to capitalize on, they will.

They've done it before with Khabib Nurmagomedov and Conor McGregor. Their feud became beyond bitter, and it was parlayed into one of the biggest events in the promotion's history.

Khabib vs. McGregor at UFC 229 in October 2018 drew about 2.4 million pay-per-view buys.

If the Nurmagomedovs and Dvalishvili avoid any further legal or criminal consequences from this series of events, you can bet that if there's any way for the UFC to match fighters from these two groups against each other, it'll happen.

And we'll all be lying to ourselves if we say the vast majority of combat sports fans won't be more interested in those fights because of this drama.

Will the UFC Still Sign Usman Nurmagomedov?

As for the UFC's interest in signing Usman Nurmagomedov, I wouldn't suspect this incident will cool its desire to sign him. If anything, it may make it all the more urgent.

There's now serious heat, drama, and storylines connecting him to someone in the UFC.

Usman, who is 22-0, became a free agent when his PFL negotiating window closed. He reportedly turned down a PFL extension worth $2 million per fight, and the UFC hasn't announced a deal.

One potential opponent could be Sterling, particularly if he moves up to lightweight. That could set up a humongous fight between those two as Nurmagomedov tries to work his way toward a title at 155 pounds.

That seems like a possibility for Sterling after he admitted to having a really tough weight cut ahead of his 145-pound fight against Kevin Vallejos on Saturday in Qatar.

Sterling and Vallejos meet at UFC Fight Night Qatar on Nov. 21 in Doha.

The only way I see this situation seriously hurting Nurmagomedov's chances of joining the UFC is if he has to serve more prison time and it keeps him out of action.

If not, this fight and the story make it even more likely that he lands with the UFC.

articles.title: AEW Dynamite Results, Winners, Live Grades, Reaction, Highlights After Full Gear 2026
articles.summary: Welcome to Bleacher Report's live coverage of the post-Full Gear episode of AEW Dynamite on November 18.
articles.body:
Welcome to Bleacher Report's live coverage of the post-Full Gear episode of AEW Dynamite on November 18.

This week kicked off this year's Continental Classic. The blue and gold brackets were revealed on Tuesday, and the first couple of matches took place on Wednesday.

Mike Bailey stepped into the ring with Nick Wayne, who, we hear, may have defeated Chris Jericho more than once.

We also saw Bandido take on his trios tag partner, Adam Page, and Samoa Joe faced Jack Perry.

Let's take a look at what happened on this week's show.

The show began with a video from after Full Gear when Will Ospreay approached Kyle Fletcher in the trainer's room. Fletcher showed some vulnerability and talked about the pressure he's been under and how he keeps coming up short.

Ospreay said he forgave him, encouraged him to get away from Don Callis, and said he would always have a spot in United Empire. Fletcher walked away without saying another word.

This was a very interesting way to go with these guys. Fletcher seems conflicted, and a babyface turn is probably what is in the works. It might take some time, but he will likely leave Callis soon.

The first match in the C2 saw Jon Moxley step into the ring with a man he teamed with at Full Gear, Orange Cassidy.

Mox is not the kind of character who can easily be toyed with, so Cassidy did not try any mind games at the start. He engaged with Moxley in a lock-up and carried it into a standard sequence of counters and holds.

It looked like OC was going to taunt Mox a bit, but he ended up nailing him with an Orange Punch and then following him out of the ring to hit a series of punches against the barricade.

When it comes to AEW, you can't find two people as different as these two. Mox is the epitome of a serious fighter, and Cassidy is a comedic character. The thing they have in common is that both guys are good in the ring and love what they do, so they had no problem finding their chemistry again.

Cassidy felt a little more aggressive than usual, which was needed if he wanted to look like he was on an even playing field with the champion.

They did a good job making it feel like these two both had a chance to win at multiple times, but a lot of people likely assumed Moxley would win or it would end in a tie, so OC getting a clean win with a pinning combination was a shocking outcome, but not an unwelcome one.

Mox was either selling the effects of Anarchy in the Arena or he was favoring his left arm.

The Orange Punch OC hit looked great. Mox sold it well, too.

Both men kicked out of each other's finisher.

Wayne and Bailey took part in the next match, which was also part of the ongoing C2 tournament. Before the match, Wayne mocked Moxley by giving a short promo from the crowd.

Speedball found himself trying not to get frustrated when Wayne used some mind games and scored a few takedowns. He was being even more cocky than usual to get under Bailey's skin.

In the early minutes of the match, it felt like the self-proclaimed winmaxxer had Bailey's number. He kept finding ways to take him down and counter his offense. Speedball did an excellent job selling for him despite being the more experienced fighter.

AEW is clearly investing a lot of time and effort into making Wayne into a star, so this was a far more competitive match than it would have been if it had taken place last year. If anything, Wayne was the more dominant of the two.

Whether you like Wayne's character or not, there is no denying the kid's skill. He ended up getting the win with a handful of tights, earning his first three points in the tourney.

The crowd is starting to buy into Wayne's character and saying his catchphrases.

One of the hand gestures Wayne did when mocking Speedball was not very SFW.

Speedball's triangle moonsault looked awesome.

The cutter Wayne hit in the middle of Bailey's shooting star press was the best spot in the match.

Ranking WWE and AEW's Most Underrated Stars of 2026 🌟

Jacob and Drew Kasper made their in-ring debut this week in a match against two local competitors who did not even get an introduction.

As expected, this was simply an excuse to show how the Kaspers work. The two guys they fought may as well have been training dummies.

It goes without saying that the Kaspers won. This was barely a match, but it gave them a chance to show off for a minute.

MCMG pitched taking on FTR and the Kasper Brothers in an eight-man match during a backstage segment.

It was fun to hear Stokely Hathaway reference training the Kaspers. It will be interesting to see if they interact with Roderick Strong at all.

MJF came out wearing his fake AEW world title and plugged his appearance in the upcoming Violent Night 2 before mocking the city of Denver.

He said Ospreay was not there tonight because he beat him up at the PPV, and he then proceeded to list off reasons why he is better than Ospreay.

This was the usual MJF promo. He manipulated facts to fit his narrative while running down his rival. He knows his strengths and leans into them, but at a certain point, you can almost predict exactly what he will say next.

Thankfully, he did not overstay his welcome. This wasn't exactly short, but it wasn't long either. This was good for what it was, but he might need to start evolving his character a bit.

The next match has been building for quite some time. Jack Perry has been trying to get Samoa Joe's attention, and he finally got it this week.

Jungle Jack was able to get the early advantage with a missile dropkick, but Joe knocked him off the apron with one big shot to stop his momentum dead in its tracks.

This match was a series of comebacks from Perry that got a bit longer each time. Joe was the more dominant by a wide margin, but there were times when he seemed impressed at Perry's resilience.

They did a good job telling the story they wanted to tell. The match was good, but not so good that they can't build on it in future encounters. They paced themselves in a way that still allowed them to have bursts of faster offence.

Joe got Perry up and hit the Muscle Buster, but Jack kicked out, shocking the Samoan Submission Machine. Joe choked him out to end the match, but he still seemed surprised it didn't end sooner.

Joe helped him up and shook his hand after it was over to show some respect for his opponent.

Perry's jacket said "Kill me" on the back.

It's too bad The Opps never took off. It feels like Joe's schedule was a factor.

Very few people have kicked out of Joe's Muscle Buster. It's been very protected most of the time, so it was a little surprising to see it happen here.

Ilja Dragunov gave a backstage interview that was interrupted by Don Callis. After Ilja turned down his offer to join the family, a match was made for Collision with Dragunov taking on El Clon for the national title.

Back in the arena, Swerve Strickland, Kofi and Austin Creed came out to celebrate winning the Trios Championships. New Level was trying to get Swerve to lighten up since the match was over.

Callis interrupted another promo and the crowd booed him as loudly as it could. He offered them spots in the DCF, but he excluded Prince Nana from the deal.

The Family surrounded the ring and prepared to attack, but Swerve had some chains they were ready to use as weapons. Don called his dogs off, but he said he is coming for the Trios titles.

This was a pretty cut-and-dry segment. Nothing special happened, but it did set up some possible title bouts for the future.

Mercedes Moné and The Cut came out to hold a combined celebration for their big wins at Full Gear. Mercedes was flanked by a couple of gold medalists from the women's freestyle wrestling team.

Jay White led the promo with some jokes about DMX. He tried to get the crowd to be quiet, but that just made everyone boo louder.

The CEO said she is the greatest women's champion and wrestler of all time. This led into the Fatal 4-Way for the TBS title bout. Mercedes was upset that she was interrupted by AZM's entrance.

AEW might have packed too much onto the show, because it did not feel like this was planned.

Queen Aminata vs. Maya World vs. Mina Shirakawa vs. AZM

AZM made the trip from Stardom to compete against Queen Aminata, Mina Shirakawa and Maya World in this TBS title bout.

Aminata has had multiple multi-woman matches since winning the belt, and she keeps coming out on top, so it appears that AEW is trying to build her reign up quickly.

This quickly turned into a hard-hitting match. All four women did some good work, but AZM and Aminata definitely stood out the most.

Unfortunately, there was a moment late in the match that stood out for all the wrong reasons. Aminata was supposed to break up a pin with a double stomp, but she was late for the takeoff, so the ref just stopped counting while the pin was still happening.

The crowd chanted "You f--ked up" a few times, but Mercedes' interference in the match changed the reaction to boos.

The mistimed pin didn't completely ruin the match, but it certainly didn't help. After hitting a brutal running kick, Aminata pinned Shirakawa for the win.

Result: Aminata defeated Shirakawa, AZM and Maya

Having two people pin one person never makes sense. The ref shouldn't even try to count.

Aminata hit a pretty stiff clothesline on Maya.

AZM mocking the CEO dance was hilarious.

Mina was on the top rope and then decided to go down to the first rope before hitting a crossbody to everyone at ringside.

Andrade gave an interview with Tony Schiavone when Fletcher came out to interrupt. They traded some insults and agreed to a match next week.

The main event was another C2 match. This time, it was partners going to battle. Page and Bandido just lost the trios titles on Saturday, and now they had to fight each other over points in the tournament.

Both men were bandaged in different places to sell the brutality of the Texas Death Match at Full Gear, but they did not waste much time locking up and trading takedowns.

Bandido and Hangman are both versatile and talented performers, and working together as partners has clearly allowed them to build some chemistry, so this was a fun encounter that highlighted the strengths of both competitors.

The crowd was cheering for everything because both guys are babyfaces, but Hangman was definitely the favorite. In a somewhat surprising outcome, Bandido was able to score the win to earn three points in the blue league.

Swerve approached Hangman backstage and implied he had plans for him down the line.

Hangman debuted new entrance music from Orville Peck this week.

This week's Dynamite was a solid follow-up from Full Gear. It addressed a lot of the important results while also setting up for the future.

The Continental Classic got off to a good start with three strong matches, two of which had outcomes some might consider upsets.

Aminata continues to look like a strong champion with another win over multiple challengers, and it feels like it's just a matter of time before she and Mercedes end up across the ring from each other.

There are a lot of stories happening in AEW right now, but the company has been doing a good job balancing all of them, so hopefully that continues.

articles.title: Charges Dismissed Against Boxer Floyd Mayweather Jr. over Bad Check in Las Vegas
articles.summary: LAS VEGAS (AP) — A Las Vegas court dismissed felony charges against Floyd Mayweather Jr. on Wednesday at the request of prosecutors, following allegations the boxer wrote a bad check to purchase a watch, according to court records.
articles.body:
LAS VEGAS (AP) — A Las Vegas court dismissed felony charges against Floyd Mayweather Jr. on Wednesday at the request of prosecutors, following allegations the boxer wrote a bad check to purchase a watch, according to court records.

A hearing in the case that had been scheduled for Thursday was canceled.

Mayweather, 49, was charged in April with theft and passing a check without sufficient funds with intent to defraud.

Prosecutors in Clark County had alleged Mayweather wrote the $200,000 check to Las Vegas designer resale store Gold and Beyond in December 2024 despite having insufficient funds in his account, according to the criminal complaint.

The Associated Press left emails, voice and text messages this week seeking comment with Mayweather's attorney, Clark County prosecutors and an attorney for Gold and Beyond.

Mayweather, a former five-division world champion, announced his retirement in 2017 with a 50-0 record. After saying earlier this year that he was coming out of retirement, he was scheduled to be in Athens, Greece, for the "Battle of the Legends" boxing match in June. The event was canceled due to a legal dispute with CSI Sports.

CSI sued Mayweather in the Southern District of New York district court alleging breach of contract for allegedly failing to fight Mike Tyson in a separate event. Mayweather denied the allegations in court documents.

Earlier this year, Mayweather was sued in New York over his alleged failure to pay rent at a Manhattan apartment and was in financial disputes with multiple jewelers.

He also filed a lawsuit in New York against his former business manager, alleging a yearslong fraud scheme.

articles.title: Floyd Mayweather's 2 felony criminal charges dismissed by Nevada prosecutors
articles.summary: The case was one of several legal and financial issues facing the Hall of Fame boxer.
articles.body:
Floyd Mayweather's felony theft and bad-check charges were dismissed Wednesday after prosecutors in Nevada declined to proceed with the case, according to court records obtained by Uncrowned.

Prosecutors requested the dismissal Monday, and both counts were dismissed Wednesday in Las Vegas Justice Court.

Clark County prosecutors filed the charges — theft involving $100,000 or more and drawing or passing a check with intent to defraud involving $1,200 or more — on April 27.

The charges stemmed from allegations that the Hall of Fame boxer purchased an Audemars Piguet watch from Gold and Beyond in December 2024 using a $200,000 check that never went through.

The criminal complaint alleged Mayweather wrote the check when he "had insufficient money, property, or credit" in his account to pay it in full. It further alleged he obtained property or services through the transaction, despite "knowing that the check would not be paid when presented."

Gold and Beyond said it gave Mayweather repeated opportunities to resolve the matter before pursuing legal action, but alleged he became unresponsive and uncooperative.

The case was among several legal and financial issues facing Mayweather. In April, the Internal Revenue Service filed a $7.3 million lien in Las Vegas against the former pound-for-pound king for unpaid taxes relating to 2018 and 2023.

Mayweather is also being sued by CSI Entertainment in New York, which alleges he received $4.65 million in advances for fights against Mike Tyson and Manny Pacquiao but walked away from the agreement.

Mayweather has been linked to a fight against Ryan Garcia on Feb. 6, although Uncrowned understands the bout is highly unlikely to materialize on that date.

articles.title: Lauren Price hopes making undisputed history could lead her to Claressa Shields showdown: 'I want the big fights'
articles.summary: Olympic gold medallist Lauren Price wants to test herself against Claressa Shields, Chantelle Cameron and Mikaela Mayer; Price will become Wales' first undisputed world champion in the four-belt era if she beats Michaela Kotaskova and hopes victory can lead to American star Shields
articles.body:
Price faced off with Shields after her last fight but no agreement has been reached for them to box.

Shields has been an undisputed champion in multiple divisions and has returned to middleweight after a period as the undisputed heavyweight champion.

Price, like Shields, won the Olympic gold medal at middleweight. She's unbeaten as a professional too. On Friday Price looks to add the now vacant WBO welterweight title to the WBA, WBC and IBF belts she already holds when she fights Michaela Kotaskova.

If she wins she will become Wales' first undisputed champion in the four-belt era.

"It hasn't sunk in yet," Price told Sky Sports . "When I turned over, that's the dream to become undisputed. I can honestly say if I achieve that on Friday then I've ticked every accolade in boxing.

"Regardless of the belts on the line, you step through the ropes and it's another fight. I just let the boxing do the talking and make sure I get that win and I win in style."

If Price does go undisputed at welterweight, moving up through divisions will be the natural next step. Shields remains a target though that fight is yet to come to fruition.

"It has to make sense on both ends," Price said. "I'm giving away weight, fine. But it was in her back garden, I wanted to come back to Wales as well.

On December 24 Chantelle Cameron and Mikaela Mayer, who vacated the WBO welterweight title, will rematch for the WBA, WBC and WBO super-welter championships. Price has an eye on fighting the winner.

"They're both great. But I believe Chantelle will win that fight again and that's a great fight for British boxing, I'm 100 percent up for it," Price said.

"I think right now obviously myself, Cameron, Mayer's in there [the pound-for-pound list] and obviously Shields. For me we're the big names and that's what I want, I want the big fights."

articles.title: WOW 34 Valencia, al rojo vivo: "Los old school vamos a cerrar una buena etapa"
articles.standfirst: Este miércoles se ha realizado la rueda de prensa oficial en los Cines MN4, donde los protagonistas principales han dejado declaraciones muy interesantes
articles.summary: Este miércoles se ha realizado la rueda de prensa oficial en los Cines MN4, donde los protagonistas principales han dejado declaraciones muy interesantes
articles.body: Este sábado 21 de noviembre, el Roig Arena se vestirá de gala para acoger WOW 34 Valencia, uno de los eventos del año para WOW FC. Este miércoles, los ocho protagonistas de las cuatro peleas principales han estado presentes en los Cines MN4 para la rueda de prensa oficial, donde han realizado los primeros careos y han dejado declaraciones muy interesantes. El combate estelar enfrentará a Luis Iván Rodríguez y a Felipe Dos Santos. El ganador de este duelo posiblemente se asegure pelear por el cinturón vacante de peso mosca en su siguiente aparición, por lo que ambos llegan con ganas. "Es un gran reto. Estoy viviendo parte de mi sueño, esto es lo que me imaginé cuando era pequeño y va a quedar en mi memoria y mi corazón para siempre", afirmaba el peleador mexicano. "Estoy muy agradecido a WOW, que me está ayudando a dar un paso para volver a la UFC. Esto es increíble", respondía el brasileño. El duelo co estelar será el que enfrente a la leyenda Enrique 'Wasabi' con César 'Goku' Arzamendia, viejos conocidos del TUF, en lo que será la pelea de retirada del español. "Yo a César lo quiero mucho, y sé que me quiere mucho, pero somos profesionales y haremos lo que tenemos que hacer", decía 'Wasabi', mientras que el Arzamendia apelaba al espíritu de los viejos rockeros. "Vamos a estar los old school cerrando una buena etapa y vamos a dar un gran show para todos". Otro de los combates principales será el que enfrente a Timur Kurbankadiev y Mor Dieye en peso ligero, donde el compañero de gimnasio de Joel Álvarez en el gimnasio Tíbet ha reconocido que "vengo para pegarme, no vengo para ver qué pasa. Voy a ser ese loco, voy a venir a partirme la cara. O se la rompo o me la rompe, son así las cosas. Si quiere striking estoy listo, y si quiere lucha también". Además, David Hervías y Luis Hernández también han prometido acción en su combate de peso medio, donde el peleador del 'The Black Panther' ha confesado que "el mensaje más importante que me ha llegado es el de mi madre. Intentaré hacerla sufrir lo menos posible. En redes sociales me pueden apoyar y lo agradezco mucho, pero la gente que realmente me importa es la que está en casa". 'El Matador', por su parte, ha puesto en valor la figura de Hervías, pero no se achanta. "No es sorpresa para nadie, yo lo sé. Es uno de los prospectos que hay en España, y eso para mí es mucha motivación". A posteriori, los ocho peleadores realizaron los cuatro careos correspondientes, y este viernes será el turno de cumplir con la báscula en el pesaje oficial y más tarde realizar el último face off. Una vez concluya ya solo queda el gran día, el sábado, donde toda la carne se pondrá en el asador en un escenario histórico para las MMA españolas.

articles.title: Anthony Joshua: British heavyweight boxer becomes dad for second time but unable to see daughter until after Tyson Fury fight
articles.summary: Anthony Joshua says ongoing training camp for his fight against Tyson Fury on December 11 means he will not see his new-born daughter until the days after the fight; "It's not ideal but she is in good hands", says Joshua, who describes daughter's arrival as a "big blessing"
articles.body:
Joshua, whose son JJ was born in 2015, is currently in training camp in Marbella in preparation for his blockbuster all-British fight against Fury on December 11 at Cardiff's Principality Stadium, and was unable to be at the birth.

Joshua says the arrival of his daughter, who has not yet been named, is "amazing" and "a big blessing" as the 37-year-old paid tribute to Nicole, the mother of both children.

While he has been able to have "many" FaceTime calls with mother and daughter in recent days, Joshua says he wished he would have been able to be there but preparations for the Fury fight mean mean he is currently "on a mission".

"It's not ideal but she is in good hands," Joshua said in an interview with The Sun .

"She's got an amazing mother, she's got amazing family round her and the people at the hospital, I heard they were amazing. I spoke to them and said thank you, so I'm pretty content at the minute that she's in good hands. But, for me, it would have been much better if I was able to be there.

"But I'm on duty at the minute and we're on a mission. I knew about this nine months ago so I made this commitment that I can't change, unfortunately, but there will be many more birthdays I'll be at, for sure."

Asked when he would likely meet her in person for the first time, Joshua said: "Probably December 12, December 13.

"I'll go and check in and rock her to sleep, let her hear my voice and let her feel my heartbeat, really. The basic stuff."

He said he would be a fully hands-on father.

"I'm going to do it all. I'm going to definitely do it all," he added.

"You might see me with some eye shadow on, some nail polish on, drinking some tea in a doll's playhouse just trying to do the right thing by her."

Joshua said he had wanted to become a father for a second time to "do something positive" after the "painful and traumatic" experience of last December's car crash in Nigeria that killed two members of his team, personal trainer Latif Ayodele, and strength and conditioning coach Sina Ghami.

"After the year that I'm coming off I wanted to do something positive," said Joshua, who was injured in the crash.

"I wanted to give JJ the opportunity to be an older brother. One day I won't be here and he'll have a sibling that he can turn to, be with and plan their future together. It's nice to have a sibling that they can lean on each other when needed, when me and his mum aren't here one day in the future."

The British boxer added: "Nicole is doing good. She is healthy. She said it was an amazing experience. She said it was easier than JJ and she's much prettier than JJ, so she's happy! She's already deeply in love with her."

articles.title: Mor Dieye, el imparable invicto que se abre paso desde Gijón: "Solamente soy un guaje que viene de las pateras"
articles.standfirst: El peleador del Tíbet, invicto, vuelve a la jaula de WOW este fin de semana
articles.summary: El peleador del Tíbet, invicto, vuelve a la jaula de WOW este fin de semana
articles.body: Desde el CD Tíbet asturiano, Mor Dieye (5-0) se abre paso. Este fin de semana, en WOW 34 Valencia, el peleador senegalés busca su sexto triunfo en un año y medio. Mientas, para el mes de diciembre, ya tiene anunciado un nuevo compromiso en PFL África. La personificación del hambre, coraje y ganas de pelear crece bajo la tutela de todo un Joel Álvarez. Y antes de enfrentarse al ucraniano Kurbankadiev este sábado, atiende a MARCA. Pregunta. ¿Cómo ha ido este campamento? Respuesta. Aquí estamos, entrenando bien, a tope. Hicimos buen campamento aquí y también el mes pasado estuvimos en Francia. Estamos a tope, entrenando bien y dando todo lo que tenemos, como siempre, como lo hacemos, 100%. Y preparando el Roig Arena. Va a ser un peleón, vamos a darlo todo. Estamos a tope, la verdad. Quiero que la gente vea a Mor Dieye de vuelta porque lleva tiempo sin pelear ya. P. Bueno… a ver… que ha sumado cinco victorias en año y medio. No será por falta de actividad… R. Así mola más. Si no estás todavía arriba, tienes que hacer más peleas y la gente te conoce más. Son así las cosas, eso pienso yo. Porque si te quedas sin pelear, nadie te va a conocer. Pero cuando peleas y peleas, la gente te conoce. P. ¿Qué sabe de su rival, Kurbankadiev? Un poco desconocido en España pero llega con un buen 6-1. R. No sé mucho de él, pero es un gran rival porque tiene buen récord. Lo que es más importante es que yo vengo para ganar. Me da igual quién me pongan. Si cojo la pelea, vengo para ganar y seguir más adelante, ¿sabes? Eso es lo que tengo en mente. P. Cuéntame eso de que te ofrecieron pelear con Gino van Steenis… R. Me da igual, me da igual, si me ponen un rival… yo lo voy a aceptar, es una pelea. Si uno pelea con los que están arriba, tú vas arriba, ¿sabes?. Por ejemplo, si yo estoy peleando con uno que tiene un 1-2… eso no me vale. Pero si me peleo con los que tienen más peleas que yo, ese me vale más. Voy a aprender más cosas, me voy a dar más nombre y tal… ¿Gino? Esa pelea también me gustaría mucho, si la hacemos en Roig Arena… tío, va a ser un peleón. Pero al final me dijeron que no, no sé qué pasó, pero bueno, eso es lo que toca. También Brian Hooi dijeron, pero nada. No pasa nada. P. Vaya carrera tiene… invicto en profesional y amateur con victorias sobre nombres como Nico Medina o Dimitri Barkaia. ¿Se habla poco de usted en el panorama nacional? R. Hay gente arriba… pero si la gente de arriba no quiere pelear contigo, está un poco más difícil, ¿sabes?. Ese es el problema. La gente dice, ¡buah!, yo no rechazo peleas, yo no rechazo peleas. Pero si le dices, ‘¡eh!, tú contra Mor’... dices, ‘¡no, no puedo porque estoy tal, estoy tal!’... Pero no es así, tío. Si te dicen contra Mor, acepta la pelea y peleamos. Es así. Los peleas son así. Pelea y si puedes ganar, ganas. Si no me puedes ganar.. nada. P. Si gana este fin de semana… no creo que le puedan decir ‘no’ a una pelea por el cinturón de WOW. R. Bueno, yo pensaba, ‘voy a pelear con Gino y después, si le gano, fijo voy a ir el cinturón’... pero al final me dijeron que no podía ser. Pero bueno, me da igual. Pero bueno, vamos al siguiente y luego lo que nos den. La verdad, después de esta pelea, si pasa, vamos a mirar cómo van las cosas... pero el cinturón es lo que quiero, es el gran sueño que tengo. Es como UFC esto, mira cuánta gente viene. Me quedé flipando en el Roig Arena en abril, tío. P. Hableme de usted… porque su historia empieza en Senegal. R. ¿Quién soy? Solamente un guaje que viene de las pateras, vine de Senegal. Empezamos haciendo lucha, vine a España, a trabajar en el mar, como albañil… de todas esas cosas trabajé. Y con las MMA empecé hace tres años. No llevo mucho tiempo. Y la verdad, gracias a Dios, todo nos va bien. Estamos ahí, queremos llegar más lejos. P. En Senegal hay una grandísima tradición de lucha… pero hasta este septiembre, con Diop, no había ningún peleador de Senegal en UFC. R. Sí, entró en la UFC y dije ’joder’. Yo quería ser el primer senegalés que entrara en la UFC. Pero el segundo no está mal. Puede ser el segundo o tercero porque hay muchos senegaleses que están ahora en las MMA. Hay mucha gente que viene poco a poco. Pero nuestro sueño es ese: llegar ahí y conseguir el contrato. Vamos a por ello. P. ¿Cómo es pelear en Senegal? R. Está complicado, cuando estuve allí… la familia me lo dijo: ‘Si quieres enfocarte en las MMA, tienes que estar en España’. Cuando viajé, estuve allí entrenando y la gente es muy, muy grande… Son de 120, 130, 140 kilos… No es como aquí. En Senegal, por ejemplo, si tienes pelea, tienes que intentar subir peso para ponerte más grande. No como aquí. Por ejemplo, en España, si tienes pelea, mi peso normal es de 84. Tienes que bajar hasta 70. Allí es diferente. En Senegal, por ejemplo, si tengo pelea y estoy pesando 80, voy a intentar llegar a los 90 para ponerme más grande. P. ¿Cómo acaba usted en Asturias? ¿Cómo acaba entrenando en el Tibet? R. Cuando llegué en patera, llegué a Canarias. Me quedé allí un tiempo. Mi padre estaba aquí y conocía a Joel. Estaba en una discoteca. Y cuando estaba en el gimnasio entrenando, le dijo a Joel que me iba a traer al gimnasio para entrenar con ellos. Y así fue. Empecé ayudándolo con boxeo, lucha y tal… pero poco a poco empecé a entrenar en MMA y Joel me dijo que me metiera a pelear. Y bueno, así. P. ¿Qué significa Joel Álvarez para usted? R. La verdad, Joel es como familia, es como un hermano. Es muy tranquilo, es muy buena gente… La última pelea, después de perder, veía los comentarios… y la gente no sabe lo que una persona sufre, lo que entrena, como da todo… y luego pierdes. Todos queremos ganar, tío, cuando uno va a pelear quiere ganar. Pero la gente no sabe eso, solamente critica. Y eso me duele. Es como si estuvieran hablando de mí, Joel es mi hermano. P. ¿Cómo es hacer sparring con él? R. Está complicado pegarlo a ese cabrón (risas, ed.), está muy complicado. El tema es que es muy alto, está fuerte, flipas… me encanta entrenar con él porque está a otro nivel y cada día aprende más cosas, aprende más técnicas, por eso me gusta mucho entrenar con él, cambiar con él golpes y hacer lucha con él. Me ayuda a llegar a otro nivel.

articles.title: WBC open door for Canelo Alvarez to challenge Britain's Willy Hutchinson for light-heavyweight world championship
articles.summary: The WBC did not put in place a mandatory challenger for new light-heavyweight world champion Willy Hutchinson; that leaves the path open for Mexican superstar Canelo Alvarez to return to 175lbs and take on Hutchinson; Canelo returned from Terence Crawford defeat to reclaim WBC 168lbs title
articles.body:
Scotland's Hutchinson won his rematch with Joshua Buatsi on November 7 to secure the vacant WBC light-heavyweight title.

Mexican superstar Alvarez reclaimed the WBC's super-middleweight belt when he outscored Christian Mbilli at the end of last month.

Although 168lbs is his natural weight, Canelo has previous boxed at light-heavyweight, beating Sergey Kovalev but losing to Dmitry Bivol.

The WBC would approve Hutchinson making a first title defence against Canelo.

"Yes, absolutely," WBC president Mauricio Sulaiman told Sky Sports .

"Canelo's win is very fresh after a year of huge difficulties, dealing with a loss against [Terence] Crawford, dealing with an injury and a surgery, then having to come back.

"The way he conquered the title and he celebrated, he's taken some time off."

WBC haven't ordered a mandatory challenger yet for the Briton, leaving that path to Hutchinson open for Alvarez.

"We will see what happens in the following days. At the convention we left that division open without a ruling. We're going to wait and not anticipate and we will see what happens in the following weeks and Canelo Alvarez certainly is a possibility [for Hutchinson]," Sulaiman said.

"If he decides to challenge at light-heavyweight, it would certainly be approved, champion against champion, if he decides to stay at super-middleweight there are certain alternatives."

The WBC president added: "I'm very proud of Hutchinson. He proved us right, there were many complaints about him fighting for the title but he proved us right and he won and he's deservedly the WBC champion."
